question: A long straight wire carries a current of $10\text{ A}$. Find the magnetic field at a point $5\text{ cm}$ from the wire. If the distance from the wire is doubled, predict the new magnetic field and justify your answer. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$.

options.C: $B=4\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}$ and it remains unchanged when the distance is doubled.
options.D: $B=8\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}$ at $5\,\text{cm}$; doubling the distance makes it $4\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}$.
